title: Rapiscan and Taronga/Macquarie 3D X-ray CT algorithms auto-detect dried shark fins, seahorses and sea cucumbers at 86-96% in a proof of concept; no customs deployment
summary: Pirotta et al. (2026) trained 3D CNN algorithms on 298 CT scans: detection 95% shark fin, 96% seahorse, 86% sea cucumber with low false alarms; authors say front-line implementation is the next step.
account: Pirotta et al., in Frontiers in Ocean Sustainability (published 8 June 2026), used Rapiscan 3D X-ray CT technology to build AI algorithms for autodetection of marine wildlife in mail and air-traveler pathways: 298 scans from 68 samples of dried shark fin, seahorse and sea cucumber, expanded with 3D convolutional neural networks and 3D Threat Image Projection, gave detection rates of 95% (shark fin), 96% (seahorse) and 86% (sea cucumber) with false alarm rates of 2%, 9% and 1%. The authors, who include Rapiscan Systems staff and researchers at Taronga Conservation Society, Macquarie University, NSW DPIRD, the Australian Museum and others, state that the paper 'demonstrates the efficacy and potential impact of AI detection tools to complement existing methods'. In The Conversation (7 June 2026) the lead authors reported success rates of 95%, 95% and 85% and wrote that 'The next step is relying on implementation of these algorithms at the front lines'; the earlier verifier found, via Earth.Org (21 May 2026, not re-fetched here), that the tool is a proof of concept with no operational customs use and that a Buenos Aires seizure it mentioned did not involve the tool. The date used is the journal publication date.
purpose: Automated detection of trafficked marine wildlife in 3D X-ray screening of mail and luggage to support customs inspection; no operational use yet.

ai_role.statement: The AI algorithms are the whole of the reported result (detection and false-alarm rates on CT scans), documented in a peer-reviewed paper and a Conversation article both written by the developers, including a Rapiscan-affiliated lead author; no seizure, inspection or deployment outcome exists, and the sole independent account (Earth.Org, per the earlier verifier) describes a proof of concept.
